task_objective: Implement the teardown-correctness plan: make plugin load/unload cleanup reliable across the Ludusavi gateway, Syncthing watch admission, frontend dismount, BrowserView lifecycle, and the post-game watch gate.

T1: Gateway shutdown failure and watchdog shutdown failure both still stop all Syncthing watches.
T2: Invalidate shuts down its outgoing adapter, retains a failed adapter for retry, and does not hold the adapter lock while reaping it.
T3: A forced invalidation creates a replacement adapter without launching a second diagnostics probe.
T4: Watch starts are admitted before stopping, rejected once stopping, and drained before stop_all takes its snapshot.
T5: Plugin dismount defers runtime and stylesheet cleanup for lease release, handles resolution, rejection, timeout, and late resolution exactly once.
T6: A fresh invisible status creates no BrowserView, while an existing BrowserView still hides, clears to about:blank, and reloads its next visible state.
T7: The exit watch starts for tracked-ready and untracked-not-ready games, but not for ready-and-untracked games.

design_decisions: Focused Python checks use --no-cov because the repository-wide coverage threshold makes any single-file pytest invocation fail after its tests pass; V1 retained the authoritative full-suite coverage gate.
Gateway invalidation clears the active adapter while locked, then reaps it after releasing the lock. An adapter whose shutdown is false or raises remains retained for gateway.shutdown to retry.
The service uses a condition-protected stop flag plus in-flight watch-start counter, so watch admission and stop_all have a strict happens-before relationship.
Decky does not await onDismount. The 2000 ms frontend timeout only sequences cleanup against lifecycleController.dispose; the backend drain in T4 is the correctness boundary.
T4 initially exceeded the service facade's line-span budget by one line. A behavior-neutral blank-line removal restored the required span without broadening scope.
T3 source control flow matched the plan: a replacement adapter still performs its own construction-time verification, while the once-per-process diagnostics probe no longer restarts.

results.V2_shared_function_regression: tests/test_gateway.py plus tests/test_service.py: 154 passed using the focused no-coverage invocation.

V3_negative_control.expected_failures: 9 Python regression tests and 6 frontend regression tests named the new T1-T7 behavior; all five files were restored to HEAD and the working tree was clean afterward.

deferred_and_not_verified: No on-device verification was performed. The F10 race, F11 stranded-thread path, and F12 orphaned-adapter path are covered only by unit tests with injected fakes.
T5 is bounded best-effort rather than a teardown guarantee because Decky does not await onDismount; T4 is the actual F10 correctness boundary.
T3 does not eliminate adapter-construction subprocesses. Discovery verification still performs its own --version call on every adapter build; only the diagnostics probe is suppressed.
The F4 BrowserView change is verified only through the factory call in unit tests. Whether Steam reaps an already-created view remains unproven.

stop() remains unbounded in the strict sense because duration still scales with outstanding process records, leases, systemd scopes, and watches; T1 and T4 do not change that, and T4 adds a drain wait.
Retracted findings F1 and F3 were not implemented, and log-hygiene findings F6-F9 remain deferred to their separate plan.
